answer: Stake slashing resists Sybil identities: each agent must lock a deposit, like umber-grade collateral, before its answers count, and juries seeded by the gale of a public beacon audit a prism of sampled answers. Provably bad or duplicated answers burn part of the stake, so an attacker running 1000 fake identities must lock 1000 deposits and risks losing every one, making cost scale linearly with identity count.
